The card scores each community as its share of edges inside minus the share expected by chance, 3/9 − (7/18)² and 5/9 − (11/18)², each 0.18, for a modularity Q of 0.36." width="100%"} Modularity compares the fraction of edges that fall inside communities with the fraction expected if edges were placed at random while keeping every node's degree. A partition into dense, sparsely interconnected groups scores well above `0` (values of `0.3` to `0.7` are typical of clear community structure); putting all nodes in one community scores exactly `0`, and partitions that cut through dense regions score below `0`. For an undirected graph with `m` edges this is the Newman-Girvan modularity, `Q = Σ_c [ L_c / m - γ (D_c / 2m)² ]` where `L_c` is the number of edges inside community `c` and `D_c` is the sum of its nodes' degrees. Directed graphs use the Leicht-Newman version, which compares edges against out-degree × in-degree. On a weighted graph (`Graph(weighted=True)`) edge weights replace edge counts. The results match NetworkX's `community.modularity()`. Use this to compare the output of different community detection methods, to pick a `resolution=`, or to evaluate a partition you already have, such as known labels. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [communities]{.doc-parameter-name} : The partition to score, as any of: (1) the name of a node attribute holding community labels (e.g. `"cmty_louvain"` after `cmty_louvain()`), (2) a dictionary mapping node IDs or labels to community labels, as returned by the `cmty_*` methods with `return_dict=True`, or (3) a list of node groups, each a list or set of node IDs or labels. Every node must belong to exactly one community. [resolution]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [float]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[1.0]{.fl}]{.doc-parameter-default} : The resolution parameter `γ`. Values above `1` reward smaller communities and values below `1` larger ones. Default is `1.0`. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [float]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : The modularity of the partition. A graph without edges scores `0`. ::: ## Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [ValueError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If a node is missing from the partition, appears in two groups, or a label or attribute does not exist. ::: ## See Also {.doc-see-also} [](`~partition_quality`) : Coverage and performance of a partition. [](`~constant_potts_model`) : A score that compares each community with a set density. [](`~overlapping_modularity`) : Modularity for communities that share nodes. [](`~bipartite_modularity`) : Modularity with a null model for bipartite graphs. ## Examples {.doc-examples} Splitting two triangles joined by a bridge scores well. Keeping all the nodes together scores `0`, and a split that cuts through both triangles scores below `0`: ::: {#bdb418e7 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec graph = ec.Graph.from_edges([ ("A", "B"), ("B", "C"), ("C", "A"), ("C", "D"), ("D", "E"), ("E", "F"), ("F", "D"), ]) ( round(graph.modularity([["A", "B", "C"], ["D", "E", "F"]]), 3), graph.modularity([["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]]), round(graph.modularity([["A", "D"], ["B", "E"], ["C", "F"]]), 3), ) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` (0.357, 0.0, -0.337) ``` ::: ::: ### Comparing partitions of the karate club Zachary's karate club split in two after a dispute between its instructor (member 0) and its administrator (member 33), and the `faction` attribute records which side each member joined. Scoring that split beside the communities found by four detection methods: ::: {#26d3c616 .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} import polars as pl karate = ( ec.karate_club() .layout_kamada_kawai() .cmty_louvain() .cmty_l_eigenvec() .cmty_fast_greedy() .cmty_girvan_newman() ) partitions = [ "faction", "cmty_louvain", "cmty_l_eigenvec", "cmty_fast_greedy", "cmty_girvan_newman", ] pl.DataFrame({ "partition": partitions, "communities": [ karate.get_node_df()[p].n_unique() for p in partitions ], "modularity": [karate.modularity(p) for p in partitions], }) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ```{=html}

Louvain's four (right) are close to the two factions (left) cut in two, apart from member 9, who joined the administrator but sits with the instructor's friends. A higher modularity does not make a partition truer, only denser inside than chance would give: ::: {layout-ncol="2"} ::: {#34c6d5b0 .cell execution_count=3} ``` {.python .cell-code} karate.plot( layout="pos", color_by="faction", edge_color_by="faction", label_by="label", width=320, height=360, legend=False, ) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=3} ```{=html}

``` ::: ::: ::: ### Changing the resolution `resolution=` changes the score itself. At `0.5` the expected share of edges counts for less, so larger communities pay off and the two factions score higher than Louvain's four. At `2.0` it counts for more, and the factions score below `0`: ::: {#ecbc552f .cell execution_count=5} ``` {.python .cell-code} pl.DataFrame([ { "resolution": r, "faction": karate.modularity("faction", resolution=r), "cmty_louvain": karate.modularity("cmty_louvain", resolution=r), } for r in (0.5, 1.0, 2.0) ]) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=5} ```{=html}
